upstream_issue_draft.title: Sage 0.13.0 can permanently classify an incoming CAT2 as external XCH after unavailable parent-spend discovery
upstream_issue_draft.reproduction: Use a fixture with the exact CAT2 receive and its parent spend. Make the first optional parent-spend fetch return None, then make it available. Assert receipt remains retryable, later resolves CAT asset, wallet inner puzzle ownership and lineage, and appears in owned inventory. No real-wallet mutation is required for regression reproduction.
upstream_issue_draft.expected: Unknown asset evidence remains unknown/retryable, not terminally treated as XCH; confirmed CAT receipt appears in correct owned CAT inventory after exact parent/lineage validation.
upstream_issue_draft.observed: Coin is asset_id=0, p2_puzzle_id=null, unspent, no lineage and excluded from unsynced-coins query; RPC history reports external XCH and exact owned coin query omits it.

safe_local_acceptance_proposal: Keep live trading and latch blocked. Independently validate exact chain receipt and use it only as isolated evidence/regression input. Test a reviewed Sage fix in a disposable fixture/profile, preserving unknown-vs-XCH semantics and retriable parent discovery. Any later original-wallet recovery/rescan or candidate rollover requires an explicitly reviewed supported path and separate authorization; no database edits, synthetic ownership injection, manual latch release, or accounting from hint/amount alone.
conclusion: Raw Sage RPC and read-only wallet DB misclassify and fail to register the chain-bound CAT receipt before CATalyst parsing. The installed-version queue excludes this stored state from normal retry, so merely waiting for more blocks does not supply a supported recovery path. Initial fallback entry remains inferred from matching source behavior, not a captured parent-fetch log. No safe complete-wallet reconciliation is available yet.
